# Reference machine: i5-8250u-sata-btrfs

Laptop. Everything below was in place for every measurement in `baseline.json` and for both profiles.

## Conditions and validity

- **Quiet baseline:** mains power, turbo off during the measurement, no other programs. With turbo on and a desktop session open, the same code varied from 3.5 s to 6.0 s (hash) and by up to 21% in the gzip ratio, and a 5% gate failed with no change in the code. With turbo off, five recordings spread by 0.2% to 0.5% (`check` 0.21%, `Compute` 0.44%, `sha256sum` 0.24%).
- **Tolerance on this machine: 10%** (`tolerance_percent` in `baseline.json`). The gate compares the median of 5 rounds with the median of the 5 recorded runs.
- **Valid reference only with turbo off.** The turbo state is not checked by the test: whoever measures turns it off (`echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo`) and back on afterwards (`0`).
- The spread between identical measurements is far below the tolerance, so this machine serves as a reference under these conditions.

| Item             | Value                                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CPU              | Intel Core i5-8250U, 4 cores, 8 threads, 1.6 GHz base, 3.4 GHz maximum                                          |
| CPU cache        | 6 MiB L3                                                                                                        |
| CPU extensions   | AVX2; no SHA-NI (the profile shows `sha256.blockAVX2`)                                                          |
| Frequency driver | `intel_pstate`, governor `performance`, **turbo off** (`no_turbo` = 1) for the whole measurement                |
| Power            | on the mains, battery not in use                                                                                |
| Memory           | 19 GiB                                                                                                          |
| Disk             | SATA SSD, 256 GB class, not a spinning disk                                                                     |
| Filesystem       | btrfs, mounted with `compress=zstd:3`, `ssd`, `discard=async`, `space_cache=v2`                                 |
| Kernel           | Linux 7.2.9 (CachyOS)                                                                                           |
| Go               | go1.26.3 (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3`); test binary built with `-trimpath`                                           |
| External tools   | `b3sum` 1.8.7 built from source with `cargo`; `zcat` from gzip 1.15                                             |
| Data             | 1 GiB of decompressed FASTQ (100-base reads, fixed seed), generated by the test; the compressed copy is 433 MiB |
| Page cache       | warm: each measurement is the best of 3 reads of a file that fits in memory                                     |
| Load             | quiet: no browser or other programs, nothing else measured at the same time                                     |

## Reproduce

```
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3
export COLLIGO_PERF=1 COLLIGO_PERF_DIR=<disk with 2 GiB free, not a tmpfs> COLLIGO_REQUIRE_B3SUM=1
COLLIGO_PERF_MACHINE=i5-8250u-sata-btrfs go test ./facts -run 'TestPerformance' -v
```

The two tests take about 15 minutes together (5 rounds each). To record a new baseline, delete `baseline.json` and run each test 5 times with `COLLIGO_PERF_RECORD=1 COLLIGO_PERF_TOLERANCE_PERCENT=10`; each run appends one measurement.

## Profiles

`cpu.pprof` and `mem.pprof` come from one run of both tests with `go test -c -trimpath` and `-test.cpuprofile`/`-test.memprofile`. The profile of a test binary records the path of the binary; it was rewritten to the bare name `facts.test` before the commit, so no user name or directory is in the files.
